newsitem.title: USA: Drug stores seen lacking size to pressure HMOs.
newsitem.headline: Drug stores seen lacking size to pressure HMOs.

text.p: Despite a wave of consolidation, U.S. drug store chains still lack the critical mass needed to force improved margins from managed care firms.

Continued competition between drug stores and other players, including mail-order pharmacy benefit managers, will keep merged drug stores from reversing the pricing pressure they have seen from managed care, health care industry analysts said.
"I don't think we've seen anywhere near enough consolidation for it to change the pricing dynamics of that industry," said Chicago Corp's Peter Costa.
Revco D.S. Inc and Big B Inc said Monday that Big B had accepted a sweetened acquisition offer from Revco in a cash transaction valued at $380 million, or $17.25 per share.
It was the latest merger to hit the drug store industry. Two weeks ago, Rite Aid Corp agreed to buy West Coast-based Thrifty PayLess Inc for $1.4 billion.
The growing clout of managed care in the United States has helped fuel the drug store mergers.
Large health maintenance organizations have squeezed drug store margins by paying lower prices for prescription drugs. Costly computer network upgrades have also driven up drug store costs.

Managed health care groups will likely find it easier to deal with the large drug store chains and steer business their way, analysts said. But the drug stores are unlikely to be in a position to demand improved margins from managed health care groups.
"I don't think the market is that tight yet," said Dain Bosworth analyst Chris Sergeant.
